summary: The paper adapts crosscoders — originally designed for cross-layer feature alignment — to track feature evolution across pre-training checkpoints of Pythia-160M and Pythia-6.9B. It combines this with attribution-based circuit tracing on structured tasks (SVA, induction, IOI) and reports evidence for a statistical-learning-to-feature-learning phase transition around step ~1000, supported by unigram/bigram KL divergence and total feature dimensionality curves. The methodology is a reasonable and, to my knowledge, novel repurposing of crosscoders; results are internally consistent and align with prior IB and induction-head findings, but experiments are confined to one model family (Pythia), one middle layer per model, and simple downstream tasks, which limits the generality of the phase-transition claim.
strengths: Genuinely novel adaptation: using crosscoders to align features across training snapshots (rather than across layers) is a natural but non-obvious repurposing that plausibly unlocks new analyses of pre-training dynamics.

Sanity checks are taken seriously: comparison to per-snapshot SAEs (matched L0/EV Pareto), sanity check for decoder-norm-as-strength via linear probes (Appendix C), completeness/faithfulness of interpretations (Appendix A), and discussion of misalignment and feature-splitting failure modes.

Connects the microscopic (features) to the macroscopic (downstream metrics) via IG attribution and two-sided ablations (top-k keep vs remove) on SVA/induction/IOI, which is more than most interpretability-of-training papers attempt.

The convergence of three independent signals — directional turning point around step ~1000, unigram/bigram KL saturating near entropy, and non-monotonic total feature dimensionality — makes the statistical→feature phase interpretation more than a single curve-shape argument.
Emergence hierarchy (previous-token → induction → context-sensitive) is a concrete, falsifiable, and mechanistically-grounded finding consistent with Olsson et al. (2022).
Two model scales (160M and 6.9B) instead of a single toy scale, and the phase-transition trend appears at both scales.

key_concerns.issue: Generality of the phase-transition claim is under-supported. Every empirical claim — the ~step-1000 directional turn, the KL-to-entropy convergence, the dimensionality dip-then-rise — is measured only in the Pythia family, only at a single middle layer per model (L6 for 160M, L16 for 6.9B), and only on SlimPajama activations. The paper frames a broad claim about 'LLM pre-training' but the evidence is one architecture, one tokenizer, one data mixture, one layer.
key_concerns.suggested_fix: Replicate the three core signals (directional turning point, uni/bigram KL, feature dimensionality curve) on at least (a) a different layer of Pythia (early and late), and (b) a second model family with open checkpoints (e.g. OLMo, LLM360/Amber, or SmolLM checkpoints). Even a partial replication would materially strengthen the phase-transition narrative.

key_concerns.issue: Statistical rigor of the headline correlations is weak. The complexity-vs-emergence-time claim rests on Pearson r = 0.309 (n=100), which is 'moderate' at best and is derived from LLM-judged (Claude Sonnet 4) complexity — a rubric whose inter-rater reliability and calibration are not reported. No seed variance, no error bars, no confidence intervals are provided for the crosscoder training itself, and single-run curves are used to argue for phase transitions.
key_concerns.suggested_fix: Report (i) multiple seeds for at least one crosscoder configuration with variance bands on Figures 4/5/8; (ii) an inter-annotator agreement or human-vs-LLM agreement check on the complexity rubric; (iii) a confidence interval or bootstrap on r=0.309; (iv) robustness of the ~step-1000 directional turn to crosscoder hyperparameters (λ_sparsity, n_features, activation function).

key_concerns.issue: The core interpretive claim — that decoder norm ‖W^θ_dec,i‖ is a faithful proxy of a feature's 'strength/presence' at snapshot θ — is load-bearing for essentially every downstream analysis, but the justification in the main text is largely intuitive (the sparsity penalty *should* zero-out irrelevant snapshots). The Appendix C linear-probe sanity check is invoked but not summarized in the main text.
key_concerns.suggested_fix: Move a quantitative summary of the Appendix C evidence into the main text (e.g. probe AUC/accuracy as a function of ‖W^θ_dec,i‖, with a null baseline), and show that the decoder-norm proxy tracks a *causal* measure of feature presence (e.g. ablation effect at that snapshot), not just probeable presence.

key_concerns.issue: Attribution-based circuit tracing uses first-order/IG linear approximations; the paper does not report the fidelity of these approximations. Without a faithfulness metric it is hard to know whether the top-k features 'necessary and sufficient' story reflects the model or the approximation. The tasks (SVA, induction, IOI) are also the field's most linearly-attributable tasks — the acknowledged limitation, but it directly bears on the 'microscopic-to-macroscopic' contribution.
key_concerns.suggested_fix: Report IG faithfulness (e.g. explained fraction of the clean-vs-corrupted logit gap by the summed feature attributions) alongside the ablation curves in Figure 7, and include at least one task where linearity is less obviously satisfied.

key_concerns.issue: The 'statistical-to-superposition transition' framing conflates two distinguishable claims: (1) that early loss is explained by n-gram statistics, and (2) that early representations are 'dense' (not in superposition). Claim (1) is directly measured; claim (2) is inferred from the total-dimensionality curve after crosscoder features are aligned, which is somewhat circular if the crosscoder is trained jointly across snapshots and reserves capacity for later features.
key_concerns.suggested_fix: Discuss whether the dip in total dimensionality at early snapshots could be an artifact of joint crosscoder training (many features that later become active must live somewhere at initialization), and provide a control (e.g. per-snapshot SAE dimensionality curves) to disentangle this.

key_concerns.issue: The paper describes what happens across snapshots but rarely explains *why*. The observed universal directional turn at ~step 1000 is presented as a striking empirical fact but not connected to any specific mechanism (loss landscape geometry, learning-rate warmup, embedding vs later-layer dynamics, tokenizer statistics). The connection to SLT/IB is asserted at the level of 'consistent with' rather than a testable link.
key_concerns.suggested_fix: Either add a targeted analysis linking the ~step-1000 event to a candidate mechanism (learning-rate schedule, gradient statistics, or comparison against LR-warmup-free training) or scope the claim to 'observed correlation with' rather than 'consistent with' the theoretical frameworks.

key_concerns.issue: Presentation issues (some may be extraction artifacts): the text repeatedly refers to 'Figure 9a/9b/9c' when Figure 3 caption is on the same content; equation formatting for L(x) has the sparsity sum outside the feature index; and the abstract and Introduction section are essentially missing/merged in the extraction, which — even discounting extraction glitches — suggests a very terse or missing abstract.
key_concerns.suggested_fix: Sanity-check figure numbering throughout the manuscript; ensure the abstract is complete and states the three empirical findings and the phase-transition claim; clean the loss equation formatting.

questions_for_authors: How sensitive are the ~step-1000 directional turning point and the total-dimensionality dip to crosscoder hyperparameters (λ_sparsity, n_features, choice of σ)? Does the turning point shift if you retrain the crosscoder on a different sparsity/EV Pareto point?
You report Pearson r = 0.309 between LLM-judged complexity and peak emergence step. What is the human-vs-Claude agreement on the same 100 features, and what is the bootstrap CI on r?

The decoder-norm-as-proxy claim underlies most conclusions. Does the decoder norm at snapshot θ correlate with a causal measure (e.g. mean absolute attribution or ablation effect) of the feature at that snapshot, and not just with linear probeability?

For the 'features exist from initialization, drop and recover around step 128, then decay' pattern — is this robust to seed and to different initialization schemes, or specific to Pythia's initialization?
How faithful is your IG attribution on SVA/IOI/induction? What fraction of the clean-vs-corrupted logit gap is explained by the summed top-k feature attributions?

Does the phase-transition picture (uni/bigram saturation → feature emergence) replicate on another open-checkpoint model family (OLMo, Amber, SmolLM)? Even a partial replication would strongly support the generality framing.
Do you observe qualitatively different feature-evolution patterns at early vs late layers, and could the reported dynamics be a layer-6/16-specific artifact?

Could the early 'compression' of feature dimensionality partly reflect that the *joint* crosscoder must reserve directions for features that only become active later? A per-snapshot SAE dimensionality curve as control would clarify.
calibration_check: Individual empirical claims are mostly scoped carefully (correlations called 'moderate', dimensionality trends called 'suggests'), but the phrase 'phase transition from a statistical learning phase to a feature learning phase' as a headline finding is broader than the single-family, single-layer evidence supports and should be either replicated or scoped down.

significance.justification: Cross-snapshot crosscoders are a useful tool that the interpretability-of-training community is likely to adopt and extend; the emergence-hierarchy and phase-transition observations are the kind of empirical anchors this subfield needs.

novelty.justification: Repurposing crosscoders from cross-layer to cross-checkpoint alignment is, per my knowledge, a first, and enables analyses that per-snapshot SAEs cannot easily do; the underlying architecture and losses are, however, largely inherited from Lindsey et al.

rigor.justification: Method is well-motivated with explicit failure-mode discussion and appendix sanity checks, but core interpretive claims (decoder norm as strength proxy, IG faithfulness, dimensionality attribution) are supported more by intuition and appendix pointers than by quantitative main-text evidence.

statistical_soundness.justification: Single-seed curves used to argue for phase transitions, no variance bands on the dimensionality/KL/directional-projection plots, headline correlation is r=0.309 without a bootstrap CI, and the LLM-based complexity rubric has no reported agreement check.

calibration_honesty.justification: Limitations section is explicit about scope (Pythia only), task simplicity, and discrete-snapshot constraints; most empirical claims are hedged, though the 'phase transition' framing in the title and contributions is broader than the evidence.

clarity.justification: Method and motivation are readable and the story is well-organized, but the manuscript has notable presentation issues (figure numbering mismatch between text and captions, equation typesetting, terse/absent abstract in this extraction) that hurt polish.

structure_compliance.justification: Standard structure (Intro, Related Work, Method, Evaluation, Downstream connection, Phase-transition analysis, Limitations, Conclusion), within a reasonable ICLR length; missing/thin abstract is the main departure.

reproducibility.justification: Model choice, layers, snapshot selection strategy, dataset, dictionary sizes, and loss are described; however, exact hyperparameters (λ_sparsity, learning rate, batch size, training tokens for the crosscoder), seed counts, and IG step counts are only partially specified in the main text.

related_work.justification: Positions the contribution against NTK/IB/SLT theory, SAE/crosscoder lineage, induction heads, and n-gram-fit prior work reasonably; a fair statement of what is inherited from Lindsey et al. vs newly contributed is present but could be sharper.

figure_quality.justification: Judging only from captions, the display items are informative and directly tied to specific claims (evolution overview, emergence-time/lifetime/projection stats, complexity-vs-time, decoder-norm trajectories, attribution/ablation curves, KL and dimensionality curves); the figure-numbering inconsistency in text is the main issue.

breadth_generality.justification: Two model scales but one family (Pythia), one middle layer per model, one dataset, and three closely-related structured tasks — narrower than the manuscript's 'LLM pre-training' framing implies.

overall_recommendation.justification: Borderline accept: methodologically interesting and empirically suggestive, but generality and statistical rigor gaps keep it from a clear accept without either replication on another model family or tighter statistics.
